Subject: Graduated ramp termination offsets and renewal-trigger discussion

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier this week. Per our conversation I've sketched a graduated-ramp prepay structure that aims to give Hepta predictable unit economics as you scale while protecting both sides from the tail risk of an early exit. Attached is a one-pager (Redwood_Term_Summary.pdf) and the ramp worksheet (HEPTA_RAMP_SCHEDULE_v3.xlsx). Key points: 

- Multi-year term: 3 years with annual prepay (you pay Year 1 upfront, then Year 2/3 annually or elect annual prepay).
- Year 1 discounted rate: 28% off list, Year 2: 18% off, Year 3: 10% off (applies to committed token bands).
- Graduated termination offsets: if Hepta terminates early we propose an unamortized prepay refund less an operational runoff adjustment (see worksheet). The refund declines on a 36-month amortization curve but with a protective administrative holdback for the first 90 days.
- Renewal-trigger clause: if usage growth exceeds the committed band for two consecutive months, Redwood can require a mid-term true-up or accelerated amortization schedule for that band (we intend this to be mechanical, not discretionary).
- Co-terming: we can co-term multiple Redwood contracts for the account; proposed approach is to credit remaining amortized value toward the new co-term instead of issuing a cash refund, unless procurement opts for a cash option (subject to cap).

Questions for you/procurement: are there internal constraints on refund mechanics (e.g., vendor escrow requirements vs. direct credit), and is a 90-day administrative holdback and 36-month amortization acceptable as a starting point?

If useful I can pull legal-friendly wording for the early-termination and co-term credit language to reduce back-and-forth.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Sofia —

Appreciate the materials. A couple of clarifying points from our side: 

1) Refund calculus: when you say "unamortized prepay refund less operational runoff adjustment" can you show the formula you intend to use? Procurement will need a deterministic calculation (no discretionary reductions).
2) Co-terming: our procurement team prefers cash refunds where possible. If you only offer credit-forwarding, we need to understand the cap and whether credits can be transferred to a sister entity in our group.
3) Renewal price protection: if we commit for 3 years, will we be guaranteed not to be charged a higher per-unit list than the Year 3 rate during the term?

Cc'ing our procurement lead Gina and turfing standard questions to procurement@heptahealth.com. If you can propose legal-friendly clause text and the explicit refund formula, that will speed things.

Hi Liam, Sofia —

Thanks for surfacing the procurement asks. I reviewed the worksheet and put explicit formulas into HEPTA_RAMP_SCHEDULE_v3.xlsx (attached). Summary of the deterministic refund calculation we propose: 

Refund = Max(0, Unamortized_Prepay - Administrative_Holdback - Early_Termination_Fee)
Where:
- Unamortized_Prepay = Committed_Prepay - Accumulated_Amortization (amortization on a monthly basis over 36 months for the committed sum).
- Administrative_Holdback = greater of (3% of committed prepay) or (amount covering 90 days of average historical spend) — protects against immediate churn costs.
- Early_Termination_Fee = flat 2% of committed prepay if termination occurs within first 12 months; otherwise 0.

Examples are tabulated in the sheet (rows A10:A20) showing refunds at months 3, 6, 12, 18, 24. We also included a co-terming example that shows a credit-forward calculation: Remaining_Amortized_Value can be applied to the new co-term contract as dollar-for-dollar credit; cash refunds are permitted but capped at 80% of the unamortized value within the first 12 months to discourage gaming the system. After 12 months, cash refunds match the unamortized value less holdback.

On renewal price protection: if you elect the locked annual prepay option for Year 2/3, we will not increase the per-unit price above the contracted year rate for those periods (we'll put that into the contract as "Price Protection" wording). Market add-ons (new premium features) may be charged separately.

I'm happy to draft the clause language and send to legal if you want a first-pass.

Regards,

Liam —

Following Neha's formulas, want to propose a commercial compromise to keep the paperwork light and close the deal: 

- Early termination within 12 months: cash refund = Min(Unamortized_Prepay * 0.80, Unamortized_Prepay - Administrative_Holdback - 2% Early_Term_Fee). This gives procurement the option of cash but limits windfall.
- Early termination after 12 months: cash refund = Unamortized_Prepay - Administrative_Holdback.
- Co-term credit path: by default we'll apply Remaining_Amortized_Value as credit to the new co-term; if procurement requests cash, the above cash rules apply.
- 90-day notice for termination and 30-day operational runout to allow KV-cache and consumption reconciliation.

I've started a DocuSign envelope with the updated term summary for signature (link below). If that looks good to you, we'll push legal to include the exact clause. 

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/REDWOOD/Envelope12345

If Hepta wants additional levers (longer amortization, different holdback) we can model scenarios but this is the baseline we prefer.

Thanks —
